_comment: Connector-specific edits to GENERATED/authored files that a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and banned anti-patterns absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one. Provenance: project_appdirect_onboard_oauth_scope_default.md (PR #74, 2026-06-07).

handfixes.summary: APPDIRECT_OAUTH_SCOPE is optional + non-secret (has a working default 'ROLE_PARTNER ROLE_PARTNER_READ'); the press marked it required + sensitive
handfixes.why: client.go/auth.go resolveClientCredentialsScope() returns the working default 'ROLE_PARTNER ROLE_PARTNER_READ' when APPDIRECT_OAUTH_SCOPE is empty and SENDS it (form.Set('scope', ...)), so the scope is not a credential and the user need not supply one. The press emitted required:true / sensitive:true in BOTH manifest.json user_config AND server.json environmentVariables. Fixed to optional + non-secret. This is the OPPOSITE of the halopsa bug (scope wired but never sent -> 401): here scope IS sent with a default. A reprint reverts both to required+secret.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Spec hook: mark OAUTH_SCOPE optional + non-secret in x-auth-env-vars metadata so the press emits required:false / sensitive:false by construction. Always read the binary's scope-resolver before classifying OAUTH_SCOPE.

handfixes.summary: MCP binary renamed appdirect-pp-mcp -> appdirect-mcp in manifest.json (name/entry_point); the press emits the -pp- name
handfixes.why: onboard re-vendors+patches manifest.json from source every run, so the -pp-mcp -> appdirect-mcp rename in name/entry_point must be re-applied after the final --resume. release.yml builds <slug>-mcp from skills.json and doesn't build a .mcpb, so manifest name/entry_point are effectively inert - but renamed anyway to honor the autotask #35 convention. A reprint/re-onboard reverts the name to appdirect-pp-mcp.

handfixes.summary: Governance reclassified method-aware: ~35 verb-less writes promoted out of Read, with explicit Credential (7) and Destructive (34) tiers (DELETE/expire = destructive; payment/password = credential)
handfixes.why: gen_governance missed ~35 verb-less writes (add/apply/change/clone/edit/execute/finalize/remove/request/notify/upload/invite/save/bill-usage/expire) plus appwise events/provisioning -> all fell to Read. Reclassified method-aware from agent-context pp:method (Read 168 / Write 118 / Credential 7 / Destructive 34): all DELETE + expire destructive; payment-method/instrument + password credential; POST-as-query (get-pricing-summary/preview-shopping-cart) stay Read. A reprint regenerates governance.md from the keyword classifier and silently demotes the writes.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Real fix is a method-aware gen_governance (classify from pp:method, not the command-name verb). Tracked in project_gen_governance_misses_verbless_writes / project_governance_rewrite_union_not_replace.

handfixes.summary: Vendor trademark owner stored without a trailing period ('AppDirect, Inc') so the non-affiliation banner doesn't double-period
handfixes.why: Owner 'AppDirect, Inc.' + the template's '.' produced 'Inc..'; the owner is stored without the trailing period (like knowbe4). A reprint with the period-terminated owner string reintroduces the double period.

handfixes.summary: doctor, the CLI error path and the MCP error path all point at `appdirect-cli auth login` instead of a nonexistent `auth setup` subcommand (issue #277, #278)
handfixes.why: This CLI's `auth` parent defines login, status, set-token and logout. It has never defined `setup`, yet three generated surfaces told operators to run it: doctor.go's auth_hint (fires when cfg.AuthHeader() is empty), helpers.go's HTTP 400/401/403 remediation, and internal/mcp/tools.go's tool-error text -- 7 occurrences in all. Cobra does not error on an unknown subcommand of a NON-root parent (legacyArgs only rejects unknown args for the root), and the generated parent runs parentNoSubcommandRunE, which returns cmd.Help() -- a nil error. So `appdirect-cli auth setup` printed help and exited 0. There was no 'unknown command' error and no non-zero exit anywhere in the journey: an operator saw a success code and was no closer to credentials, and because these are agent-first CLIs with typed exit codes, an agent performing setup read exit 0 as success and carried on unauthenticated. The hint fires exactly when it matters -- fresh install, rotated secret, new machine, expired token. This skill emits no auth_instructions field, so these hints are the only setup guidance it gives. The replacements name the real command and, in doctor, the variables `auth login` actually reads: APPDIRECT_CLIENT_ID and APPDIRECT_CLIENT_SECRET (plus the optional APPDIRECT_OAUTH_SCOPE), taken from the login command's own env fallbacks rather than composed. Reported by @geekbrownbear, who verified halopsa and ninjaone live against an empty config (PR #277) and filed appdirect/crowdstrike as issue #278; the fleet scan that found the other two surfaces and confirmed only these four connectors are affected was done during triage. GENERATOR-class defect: until the press is fixed, a reprint reintroduces all 7 strings and these asserts guard them. Bug-fix-only: no new flag, command, or output field.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: DONE UPSTREAM: mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#4315 closed as completed 2026-08-25 ('already fixed on current main': the oauth2 auth hint names `auth login` since PR #2875, merged 2026-06-08, first shipped press v4.25.0); this hand-fix stays active until a reprint absorbs it, and the helpers.go and MCP tool-error surfaces must be re-checked at that reprint because upstream's closure named only doctor's auth_hint and the usage error; do NOT cite #4315 as open. Encoded there: Derive the auth hint from the subcommand set the connector actually generates instead of the fixed "Run '<cli> auth setup' for credential setup steps." string in internal/generator/generator.go. 52 of 56 connectors do define `auth setup`, which is why the hard-coded string went unnoticed; the four OAuth client-credentials connectors that scaffold `auth login` instead (appdirect, crowdstrike, halopsa, ninjaone) each shipped it 7 times. The same string is emitted into three surfaces -- doctor.go's auth_hint, helpers.go's 400/401/403 remediation, and the MCP server's tool-error text -- so a generator fix must cover all three.

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282.

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For appdirect the manifest gained: APPDIRECT_BASE_URL, APPDIRECT_TOKEN_URL. server.json gained: APPDIRECT_BASE_URL, APPDIRECT_TOKEN_URL. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: APPDIRECT_BASE_URL, APPDIRECT_TOKEN_URL. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: APPDIRECT_NO_CONFIG_WRITE makes every credential write a no-op (token cache included) while leaving the `auth logout` erase working, and the MCP server honours it too (issue #270)
handfixes.why: Issue #270, raised by @Xenith-B off the back of #266. #266 stopped env-supplied client credentials reaching disk; the MINTED access token still landed in ~/.config/<tool>-cli/config.toml in cleartext and there was no supported way to turn that off. Their workaround was `--config NUL`, which is OS-specific, undocumented, makes doctor report a false 'not configured', and - the part that matters most - does not cover the MCP servers at all, because internal/mcp resolved its own hardcoded config path and ignored --config. Three deliberate boundaries make this switch honest rather than merely quiet. (1) ClearTokens keeps calling save() directly: it is the ERASE path, and routing it through the guard would make `auth logout` silently inert, which is a worse defect than the one being fixed. (2) `auth login` and `auth set-token` REFUSE and name the variable rather than reporting a save that did not happen - a false success is the same defect class as a doctor that says credentials are fine without checking. (3) newMCPClient now resolves through config.Load(""), the resolver the CLI uses, so the MCP server honours both APPDIRECT_CONFIG and this switch; that is the half the issue says is uncovered today. The variable is declared on all three install channels because for a Claude Desktop install the manifest prompt is the ONLY channel that can set an environment variable. Class C, new documented surface. GENERATOR-class: a reprint drops the switch entirely and silently restores the plaintext token cache.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit <PREFIX>_NO_CONFIG_WRITE (or an equivalent) as part of the standard config surface, with the same three boundaries: the erase path exempt, explicit save commands failing loudly rather than no-oping, and the MCP server resolving its config through config.Load("") instead of a hardcoded home-relative path. The hardcoded path in internal/mcp/tools.go is a generator defect in its own right - it makes --config and <PREFIX>_CONFIG inert for every MCP install on every connector.

asserts.contains: | `auth login` / `auth set-token` | Refuse, naming the variable, instead of reporting a save that did not happen. |

handfixes.summary: The generator's hidden Cobra alias `create` is removed from the 3 commands listed in `why` whose POST deletes, cancels, disables, stops, rolls back or otherwise destroys or disrupts something, so `<parent> create` no longer runs them
handfixes.why: cli-printing-press gives a POST endpoint command the hidden alias `create`. On these commands the POST is destructive, so an agent that guessed the conventional verb (`<group> create`) ran the destructive call, and the alias appeared nowhere in help, agent-context or governance.md. Reproduced on origin/main 6416a241b against a local fake server: `maxio-cli subscriptions purge-json create sub_123 --ack 1` sent POST /subscriptions/sub_123/purge.json, `sentinelone-cli reports create` sent POST /reports/delete-reports and `tactical-rmm-cli agents shutdown create agent-42` sent POST /agents/agent-42/shutdown/. Fleet gate: tools/maintainer/check_command_tree.py, which walks the real cli.RootCmd() tree (137 such commands in 28 connectors on 6416a241b, 0 after). The canonical command names are unchanged; only the alias goes. A reprint re-adds it: remove it again. TestDestructiveCommandsDoNotAnswerToCreate fails while the alias is present. Commands here: appwise events (POST /appwise/v2/data); products delete-image (POST /products/v1/resources/image/delete); shopping-carts items delete-shopping-cart (POST /shoppingCarts/{shoppingCartId}/items/delete).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: emit the `create` alias only for operations that create something.

handfixes.summary: --dry-run never mints a token or changes stored credentials: neither the client's automatic client-credentials mint nor `auth login --dry-run` sends the client secret to the token URL, and `auth set-token --dry-run` and `auth logout --dry-run` neither save nor clear anything
handfixes.why: tools/maintainer/class_harness.py write-safety found every --dry-run of a write command putting one request on the wire: authHeader ran before the dry-run branch and, with no cached token, POSTed the client ID and secret to the token URL and cached the token, while the generated comment and the docs say a dry run sends nothing. `auth login` minted through its own path and ignored --dry-run, and `auth set-token` and `auth logout` saved and cleared credentials under --dry-run (found by Codex review round 1). Same fix shape as connectwise-rmm, sophos-central and watchguard (dry-run-never-mints). TestDryRunNeverMintsAToken, TestAuthLoginDryRunSendsNothing and TestAuthSetTokenAndLogoutHonorDryRun count requests to a stub token server (each with a live control that proves the probe reaches the mint) and fail on the generated code.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press fix: client.go.tmpl should skip the client-credentials mint when DryRun is set (the dry-run preview already uses cached material only), and auth.go.tmpl's login should honor the root --dry-run flag.

handfixes.summary: Every token request (auth login, the automatic client-credentials mint and the refresh grant) goes through cliutil.OAuthTokenHTTPClient, which follows same-origin redirects only, so the client secret never reaches a host a redirect from the token URL names
handfixes.why: Owner decision on PR #441 (finish the auth-wire class). `auth login` (through http.DefaultClient) and the automatic client-credentials mint and refresh grant (through c.HTTPClient, whose CheckRedirect follows a 307 to another host) replayed the token request body, the client secret included, to whatever host a redirect from the token URL named. Printed before press 4.33.5, which routes every token request through cliutil.OAuthTokenHTTPClient (a token client that follows same-origin hops only); this back-ports that file verbatim and uses it at the same call sites. TestAuthLoginRefusesATokenRedirectToAnotherOrigin and TestTokenMintRefusesARedirectToAnotherOrigin failed on the previous commit (the second host received the token request) and pass now. The host compare is also hardened (see the newer-print entries): an IP literal compares exactly, IPv6 zone included; a DNS name folds ASCII case only.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: auth.go.tmpl and client.go.tmpl in press 4.33.5 already route token requests through cliutil.OAuthTokenHTTPClient; oauthTokenSameOrigin should compare IP literals exactly (zone included) and fold ASCII case only for DNS names.

handfixes.summary: One decoded output funnel for every server text the client shows: maskCredentialText (every API error, transport error, displayed URL and --dry-run parameter goes through it) still masks each held credential as written and URL-escaped, then withholds the WHOLE text if any held value survives in any view reachable by undoing control/format characters, JSON and JavaScript escapes, percent escapes at any depth, HTML entities, markup tags, and base64/base64url/hex runs at every alignment (cliutil.FunnelWithhold, shared byte-identical across the fleet). The held set is every value the masks cover plus the part after a scheme word and both halves of a base64 id:secret pair (Basic auth, composed keys). Surfaces funnelled here: the API error body (checked whole before the 4096-byte display cut, then again as shown); the OAuth client-credentials token endpoint's error body; the token refresh endpoint's error body. The `auth login` token exchange (internal/cli/auth.go mintClientCredentialsToken) funnels its error body with the client secret it sent. Round 3 (owner-approved structural pass): the decoder searches every view breadth-first over one fixed set of steps (control-character drop, JSON and JavaScript escapes, the identity escape as its own step, percent, HTML entities, tag strip, base64 at four alignments, hex at two), matches every view, the original included, before any filter, keeps every view a step makes (a literal backslash survives), deduplicates, and is capped by total work (512 times the input plus 4 MiB; text over 1 MiB or past the cap is withheld). Every value a funnel call is given is held process-wide (cliutil.FunnelHold), and the client holds its credentials when built and its resolved auth header on every request. Two error-only backstops withhold any held value: every command error before Cobra prints it plus every JSON/agent error envelope (internal/cli/secret_funnel_cli.go), and every MCP error result and handler error through the outermost tool middleware (cmd/<mcp>/secret_funnel_mcp.go). Success output is never funnelled.
handfixes.why: class_harness.py secret-echo (Step 3.1, PR #436) drives the built CLI and MCP server against a fake server that reflects each configured credential in every encoding; on origin/main this connector printed the credential HTML-entity-encoded, JSON-escaped, double URL-encoded or base64 (the generated masks cover only the raw, QueryEscape and PathEscape forms; press issue #5145). Matching encoded needles one at a time never converged (saas-alerts and cisco-meraki review loops), so the fix is a decode-then-check backstop that withholds the whole text and fails closed (text over 4 MiB, a decoding chain that does not settle in 32 rounds, or work past the budget is withheld). Classification is kept: the plain withheld notice avoids every word the auth-error classifiers match, and a withheld text that itself read as an auth failure gets a notice that says so (an HTTP 400 'invalid token' answer echoing the token keeps its auth exit code). Codex round 1 (2026-10-23) added that, the fail-closed depth bound (a text-like layer left at depth 8 withholds), the JavaScript escapes \v, \0 and the identity escape, a bounded \u{ search, and the token-endpoint error bodies outside the client. Known limits: values under 8 characters are only masked as written; case-changed, split-and-interleaved or otherwise transformed (compressed, encrypted) echoes are not reconstructed. A reprint that drops these edits fails class_harness.py secret-echo in CI and these asserts.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: cli-printing-press issue #5145 (encoded credential echo). The generated maskCredentialText should end in a decode-then-check backstop over every held credential, and the error-body and token-endpoint paths should check the whole body before the display cut.

Tests: TestNothingPrintsBeforeTheChokepoint (black-box, CLI and MCP), TestLoadHoldsURLCredentialsAndTheOverriddenFileLayer; prove_bb.sh startup-order, url-holds, file-layer-holds. handfixes.summary: A credential goes only to the scheme, host and port configured for it: every API request and the bearer token to the API base URL's origin; the token URL's origin (when it differs) only receives POST <token path> carrying no bearer token; every redirect hop stays on the origin of the request it follows; a non-ASCII or unparseable host never matches; `auth login`'s own token client is pinned the same way
handfixes.why: Work-order credential rule (host pinning). Each AppDirect marketplace is its own host, and the token URL is configurable separately (APPDIRECT_TOKEN_URL), so the guard has two pins (the pax8 shape) over action1's one-origin guard. Applied through registerClientHook (every CLI, novel and MCP client) and one anchored line in root.go oauthHTTPClient (tools/apply_credential_rules.py).

handfixes.summary: The last check before config.toml is written reads back the exact bytes whatever shape produced them (an agentcookie-managed save marshals the whole configuration) and refuses a file that repeats a held value or the configuration's credentials in any form; every header is judged by name, by credential shape and by the output chokepoint's full matcher (cliutil.EchoesValues), so a header holding a credential's base32 is left out. Under agentcookie a minted token stays in process memory.

The generated TestAgentcookieMarkerKeepsCredentialsInConfig asserted the old behavior and now asserts the refusal (tools/apply_credential_rules.py). Seen failing: seen/r1-credential-persisted-outside-the-store-seen-failing.log.

handfixes.summary: The output chokepoint matches by decoding, not by enumerated spellings: every hex-digit run is a byte in decimal, hex, octal or binary whatever separates the runs (byteTokenEchoes); a held value under eight characters is searched in every run of each 4-, 5- and 6-bit alphabet decoded at all eight bit alignments, base85 at all five group alignments and radix runs as one number (shortAlphabetEchoes); a held number is matched as its value in any notation (numericEchoes). The byte-escape pre-check counts hex digits (a superset of what its decoders read). The funnel's needles are cached per held list.

handfixes.why: Docs fix approved 2026-11-03, following PR #502. OpenAI's MCP docs (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/extend/mcp) say the ChatGPT desktop app, Codex CLI and the IDE extension support MCP servers, add them as STDIO, and share MCP configuration; ChatGPT on the web uses remote MCP through plugins and does not read local Codex config. The old text listed ChatGPT plans, said ChatGPT connects only to remote servers, and on the reprinted connectors told users to host the connector over HTTPS for a Developer Mode connector and Copilot Studio; SECURITY.md pauses HTTP mode until each connector is reprinted. README.md, mcp-install.md and page.json are regenerated by msp-skills-publish onboard.py, whose template still writes the old ChatGPT text, so without this entry a re-onboard or reprint silently restores it.
